questions.question: What definition of renal failure is more correct?
options: it is autointoxication of the organism that is associated primary with damage of the structural elements of the parenchyma by infectious or toxic factors;
it is such a change of renal function, which causes a disturbance of the state of the internal environment.

questions.question: Specify the types of renal failure:
What form of renal failure includes renal diabetes, cystinuria, phosphate diabetes which are caused by inheritance of the corresponding genetic defects?
Specify the causes of acute renal failure type of “shock kidney”:
options: Crush syndrome, a disease occurring with uncontrollable vomiting and profuse diarrhea, leading to dehydration;
poisoning by carbon tetrachloride, bilateral obstruction of the urinary tract by stones.

questions.question: Specify the reasons leading to acute renal failure type of “vascular obstruction”?
options: acute glomerulonephritis, thrombosis and embolism of the renal arteries;

questions.question: Specify the reasons of acute renal failure type of “urological obstruction”?
options: unilateral blockage of the urinary tract by stones; c) anaerobic infection;

questions.question: Specify the stages of acute renal failure:
options: oligo-anuric, initial, recovery of diuresis and polyuria, reconvalescence.

questions.question: What is the stage of acute renal failure syndrome is characterized by development of uremia?
What factors reduce the filtration in the renal glomerulus?
options: reducing the hydrostatic pressure in the glomerular capillaries, increasing the oncotic pressure of the blood, increasing intrarenal pressure, reduction of the filtering surface;
increase in hydrostatic pressure in the glomerular capillaries, decreased oncotic pressure of the blood, reducing the intrarenal pressure, increased filtration surface.

questions.question: How changes the hydrostatic pressure in the renal glomeruli when constriction of the renal artery and afferent arterioles?
How changes the filtration pressure when spasm of efferent arterioles?
Diffuse glomerulonephritis is accompanied by:
options: increased permeability of glomerular basement membrane;
decrease in the permeability of the glomerular basement membrane.

questions.question: Acute diffuse glomerulonephritis is accompanied by increase in glomerular filtration process?
What changes reduce the hydrostatic pressure in the renal glomeruli?
options: increased blood pressure, increased cardiac output, increased blood volume, increased plasma volume;
decreased blood pressure, decreased cardiac output, decrease in blood volume, decreased plasma volume.

questions.question: What factors contribute to increased water reabsorption in the renal tubules?
options: increased production of ADH, increased sensitivity of epithelium of the renal tubules to ADH, increase of reabsorption of the osmotically active substances from tubules;
the decrease in production of ADH, reducing the sensitivity of epithelium of the renal tubules to ADH, reducing reabsorption of osmotically active substances from tubules.

questions.question: What are the factors directly related to the defeat of tubular apparatus of the kidney in acute renal failure?
options: infectious-toxic, hypoxia of the nephron, action of metabolites and breakdown of tissues (myoglobin, hemoglobin, etc.);
impaired renal lymph circulation, increase in intrarenal pressure.

questions.question: What is determined by larger degree of decreased urine output than the degree of reduction of glomerular filtration at background isostenuria in oligo-anuric stage of acute renal failure?
options: that oliguria in acute renal failure is associated not only with the change of filtration, but also with the development non-selective resorption of the ultrafiltrate of tubules;
that the crucial in the development of oliguria in acute renal failure belongs to a violation of resorption of the tubular ultrafiltrate.

questions.question: What factors reduce renal blood flow in the early stages of the action of nephrotic poisons?
options: reduction in energy production in the cells of tubular epithelium;
increasing the tonus of afferent arterioles of renal glomeruli;

questions.question: What factors can cause anuria?
options: severe trauma, significant pain stimuli, bend or compression of the ureters;
denervation of the kidney, a drop of hydrostatic pressure in glomerular capillaries up to 50 mm Hg.

questions.question: What factors can cause a hyponatriuresis?
options: increase in glomerular filtration rate, a decrease in aldosterone production, reducing the sensitivity of cells of the tubules to the aldosterone;
increased production of aldosterone, decrease in glomerular filtration rate, an increase in the sensitivity of cells of the tubules to the aldosterone.

questions.question: What changes lead to a decrease in sodium reabsorption in the renal tubules?
options: increase in the sensitivity of cells of the tubules to the aldosterone.

questions.question: The combination of hypostenuria with polyuria indicates on the primary lesion of the nephron structures, such as:
Reducing the elimination from the body of the urea and creatinine leads to:
What violations of plasma are typical for oligo-anuric stage of acute renal failure?
Hyperkalemia in acute renal failure is associated with violation of processes such as:
options: filtration and reabsorption of potassium, reabsorption and secretion of potassium, increased protein anabolism processes;
filtration and secretion of potassium, increased protein catabolism.

questions.question: What are the factors associated with the development of hyponatremia in the third stage of acute renal failure?
options: increasing sodium excretion from the body, thinning (hemodilution) of blood, increased transition sodium from the extracellular space into the cell;
sharp drop of its filtration in third stage of acute renal failure, output of sodium from cells to the extracellular space, delay of potassium in the body.

What is the reason of hyponatremia in chronic renal failure?
options: decrease in the sensitivity of the epithelium to the ADH, decrease in the rate of filtration of sodium in functioning glomeruli;
decrease in the sensitivity of the epithelium to the aldosterone, increased filtration rate of sodium in the functioning glomeruli.

questions.question: Can extra- as well as intracellular hyperhydration develop when acute renal failure and chronic renal failure?
What is the reason of the acidosis in renal failure?
options: reduction in the secretion of hydrogen ions in the tubules, decrease in filtration of phosphates, increased loss of bicarbonates;
increased secretion of hydrogen ions in the tubules, increased filtration of phosphates, decreased excretion of bicarbonates.

questions.question: What accounts for dyspepsia (loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) in chronic renal failure and uremia?
options: diselectrolytemia, increased formation of ammonia in the gut.

questions.question: Uremia is characterized by:
options: polycythemia, leukopenia, increase of platelets per unit volume of blood, hypercalcemia.

questions.question: Specify the reasons of the prerenal form of acute renal failure:
options: thrombosis and embolism of renal vessels;

questions.question: How changes the diuresis with a decrease in reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubules?
The tubular acidosis is a consequence of changes in the function of the nephron:
How changes filtration when selective increase in tonus efferent arterioles of renal glomeruli?
How changes the hydrostatic pressure in capillaries of the renal glomeruli when increases in tonus of afferent arterioles?
How changes the diuresis when decreases of reabsorption of glucose in the renal tubules?
What is the leading pathogenetic factor of prerenal form of acute renal failure?
options: difficulty of removing of urine from urinary tract.

questions.question: Which are pathogenetic factors lead to reduction of renal blood flow in the development of prerenal form of acute renal failure?
options: hypervolemia, lowering tonus of afferent arterioles;
hypovolemia, increased tonus of afferent arterioles, violation of hemorheological properties of blood.
